assumptions: The quantifier class is exactly as defined: P sees the cycle's own labels and site tags and nothing else. A criterion permitted to inspect the rest of the federation, or several cycles jointly, is NOT covered and is a different question.
attrs.evidence: Suppose P is sound and complete. Let F be K₄ all-≠ in three matchings; ¬fidelity(F), so by completeness some cycle C of F satisfies P. Let F' be the federation whose constraints are exactly C's edges with the same relations and site tags. C is a cycle of F', so FAIL_P(F') holds. But F' is a single ≠-cycle: 3-colourable, with every site a sub-multiset of a matching, so fidelity(F') HOLDS — contradicting soundness. ∎ The load-bearing step is checked: all 7 of K₄'s simple cycles keep fidelity when extracted. The |D|=2 contrast is checked too — an unbalanced split cycle STILL fails fidelity when extracted, which is exactly why 'split and unbalanced' is a valid cycle-local criterion there.
attrs.prior_art: Not searched. The statement is elementary once the quantifier class is fixed; the point of fixing it is that the previous informal version could not be attacked.
attrs.review_focus: Proved ONLY for the quantifier class it names. A criterion permitted to inspect several cycles jointly, or the rest of the federation, is untouched — and that is a strictly larger and more interesting class.
attrs.statement: Define a CYCLE-LOCAL CRITERION as a predicate P on (labels(C), sites(C)) — the relations and site tags along a cycle, in order, and nothing else about the federation containing it — inducing the test FAIL_P(F) := ∃ a cycle C of F with P(labels(C), sites(C)). Then at |D| = 3 over {=, ≠} there is NO cycle-local criterion P that is both sound and complete, i.e. satisfies FAIL_P(F) ⟺ ¬fidelity(F) for every federation F.
attrs.superseded_by: FED-Q2-DK-LOCALITY (all k ≥ 3) and FED-Q2-BOUNDED-LOCALITY (all bounded sizes s)
